resolutions.question: 17675 vs 17670
resolutions.answer: The accounting list is built from classRecords, which holds exactly ONE SourceRecord per DISCOVERED file (estate-capture-v1.mjs:227, census.flatMap over classRecords). Two classes of ledger entry therefore can never appear in it: intermediate versions of files that mutated mid-run (the memory .md at 6,606 then 8,956 bytes; the cursor sync manifest), and adhoc sources under /tmp that discovery does not cover (the two replication canaries). This is a mechanism, not a restatement.
resolutions.architecturalConsequence: The accounting model is DISCOVERY-BOUNDED by design. It will under-count any source that mutates during a capture run. That is a real property worth knowing before the model is trusted for completeness claims.

resolutions.question: 3665 apparent encryption gap
resolutions.answer: NOT A GAP. It is content deduplication: 17675 observations resolve to 13998 unique objects (1.26 observations per object). objectsAudited=14005 covered 100 percent of the spool.

resolutions.question: 113 refused vs 118 quarantined
resolutions.answer: 118 register entries = 113 unique identities + 5 duplicates across exactly 3 sources (x2, x3, x3). Independently reverified by the integrator using the real fields (sourceRootId + relativePath); an earlier integrator check using sourceNativeId returned UNKNOWN for all 118 and proved nothing. Set arithmetic: |quarantined| = |refused| = |intersection| = 113; both differences 0.
resolutions.cause: Three Claude session files were re-scanned as they grew during capture. Every scan is recorded in the register; only the latest is counted in accounting -- the same discovery-bounded behaviour as the 5-delta, arrived at independently.
